significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish both a form-(iii) invariance—“a shared, language-independent magnitude subspace regardless of how [numbers] are lexicalized”—and a computational ordering in which “arithmetic operates over this shared code before language-specific verbalization,” thereby predicting aligned magnitude geometry and comparable causal disruption across languages and numeral forms. This would provide a phenomenon (form-invariant numerical representations and transfer) and a mechanism (arithmetic consuming the shared code before language-specific output), constraining more than the basic shared-representation hypothesis discussed in multilingual work such as Wendler et al.'s “Do Llamas Work in English?” and the numerical geometry studied in Engels et al.'s “Language Models Use Trigonometry to Do Addition.” A verified-false result would meaningfully rule out the joint universal-code/pre-verbal-arithmetic account, although it would not by itself distinguish language-specific codes from partial sharing or representation changes by layer; the two branches are nevertheless determinate. In the topic-substitution check, the generic multilingual-representation topic would not retain this score because it lacks the claim-specific invariance across digits and words and the asserted computation-before-verbalization ordering.

reach.justification: The transferable handles are the “shared magnitude subspace,” the “form-invariant magnitude manifold,” and a cross-form magnitude probe, together with ablation of the shared subspace as an intervention target. These are primarily post-hoc diagnostic and causal-analysis tools rather than ex-ante failure forecasts, but the claimed invariance is a relation that predicts what should be recovered after recalibration on another multilingual model, rather than merely prescribing an open-ended search procedure. The hypothesis asserts scope across numeral forms and languages, so its principal downstream users would be multilingual interpretability researchers and model auditors assessing arithmetic consistency, although it supplies no explicit deployment gate or demonstrated scope across architectures, scales, or training regimes. The topic-substitution check lowers the generic topic to its median reach: the score above that baseline comes specifically from the reusable magnitude-manifold/probe handle and its asserted cross-form invariance.
